The bump aligns with the LawFirm OS architecture principle that the lake must track substrate contract authority without stale SHA drift.
diff_review_summary: Old contract_sha: 35deefb5081b6b8d3ace4ad78ecd58c14965394a (4 commits behind substrate HEAD). New contract_sha: dfacbb5e29a85834e37bb393bc45e80ab2e3a204 (current substrate HEAD = local HEAD). generated_at updated to 2026-05-14T20:00:00Z. New field pin_rationale added explaining the bump. No governance keywords removed. No public symbols affected (JSON config file). Net effect: eliminates SHA drift; lake and substrate are now aligned.
why_merge_not_sufficient: The contract lock is a single pinned SHA value; there is no meaningful merge between two SHA identifiers. The old SHA must be replaced with the new one. The old SHA is preserved in git history and in the pin_rationale field.
replacement_justification: The old SHA was 4 commits stale against the substrate origin/main HEAD. Keeping the stale SHA would allow the Exception Lake to import governance contracts that pre-date the SACP + managed-patch-preservation integration, violating the substrate-authority principle. The bump is provenance-verified: the new SHA is the current local substrate HEAD, confirmed by git log before the bump.
alternatives_considered: Option B: Leave old SHA with a prose comment documenting why drift is acceptable. Rejected because prose comments in JSON are non-standard and the lock validator would still flag drift indefinitely.
Option C: Remove contracts.lock.json and rely on runtime detection. Rejected because the lock provides a static integrity gate checked during pytest; removing it degrades the safety guarantee.
